members.reason: ["Held Executive Order 6730 of May 30, 1934 (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6730-revised-code-fair-competition-the-iron-and-steel-industry.txt) approves the Iron and Steel code 'as amended' as a revised code and says that revised code is \"to become effective on June 11, 1934, prior to which effective date the Code of Fair Competition approved August 19, 1933, shall continue in full force and effect\". That is a possible superseding event before June 14, 1935 and, if it supersedes, the first end of what it reaches; a June 14, 1935 end would contradict it.", "Executive Order 6730 is not in this packet's dossier evidence (the chain has no events and the 'generic_refs_excluded' count is 221), so it cannot be cited as an ending or later event; the lookups missed it because they match 'Code of Fair Competition for the ...' and 6730 says 'Code ... of the Iron and Steel Industry'.", "To unblock: put Executive Order 6730 into the evidence (a packet or reviewed ACT record) and decide whether the revised code replaced the August 19, 1933 approval on June 11, 1934 or only amended it."]

["Clause 1 creates \"a wall paper manufacturing industry committee\" \"to cooperate with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency\", composed of five industry representatives and three non-voting members appointed by the Administrator. The order states no duration, and no held source shows the committee being constituted, continuing or ending.", "A committee beside an approval needs its own end or a block. The shared analysis says NRA administration continued to April 1, 1936, so S.J. Res. 113 section 2 (code approval and enforcement) does not by itself establish that a body cooperating with the Administrator ended on June 14, 1935, and nothing held shows it was a creature of the code alone.", "To unblock: a held source on the committee's constitution or dissolution, or a reviewed ruling that a section 3(a) condition of this kind falls with the approval."]

["Clause 1 requires that \"a Code Authority be created to cooperate with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency\", of nine industry representatives and three non-voting members appointed by the Administrator. The order states no duration, and no held source shows the Code Authority being constituted, continuing or ending.", "A committee or authority beside an approval needs its own end or a block; the NRA administration it cooperates with continued to April 1, 1936 (shared analysis), so S.J. Res. 113 section 2 does not by itself establish an end on June 14, 1935.", "To unblock: a held source on the Code Authority's constitution or dissolution, or a reviewed ruling that a section 3(a) condition of this kind falls with the approval."]

["Conditions (2) and (3) (a hearing by the Administrator within 90 days of the code's effective date on the adequacy of minimum wages, and a further presidential order that would modify the approval) run from the code's effective date, which no held source states, and the order gives no other date.", "Held Executive Order 6620-B of February 26, 1934 (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6620-b-code-fair-competition-for-the-hotel-industry-modification-executive.txt) modifies the November 17, 1933 approval \"by striking therefrom the conditions numbered two (2) and three (3)\". That is the first end of those two conditions, earlier than June 14, 1935, but Executive Order 6620-B is not in this packet's dossier evidence (the chain has no events), so it cannot be cited as an end.", "To unblock: put Executive Order 6620-B into the evidence; then clauses 2 and 3 end February 26, 1934 by modification of the approval, and the approval itself and condition 1 end June 14, 1935 by the repeal."]

["The condition grants \"all manufacturers of Knitted Outerwear for infants and children, sized from infancy to and including age fifteen\" \"a stay from the provisions of this code, until determination by the Administrator, after such hearing as he may deem necessary, as to whether or not they are to be included in this code\". The stay ends on a determination, not a date; no held source shows a determination, so the stay's own end before June 14, 1935 is neither established nor excluded.", "A search of the held order texts for 'Knitted Outerwear' finds no later order naming this code or the stay. A stay pending a determination is a contingent command that needs its own end or a block; absence of a held determination does not show that none was made.", "To unblock: a held record of the Administrator's determination, or a reviewed ruling that the stay, as a section 3(a) exception, falls only with the approval."]

["The approval is \"on condition that each of the trade associations representing the thirty-nine (39) subdivisions of this Code shall amend its constitution ... within thirty (30) days after the effective date of this Code\" and that the code authority recommend definition changes \"within sixty (60) days from the effective date of this Code\". No held source states the code's effective date, so neither window can be dated, and no held source shows whether either condition was met.", "These are commands with deadlines, and a deadline is not an end; without a held effective date they cannot be given an own-terms end before June 14, 1935 or shown to run past it.", "To unblock: the Machinery and Allied Products code's effective date from a held source (the code text or an NRA release) and evidence on performance of the two conditions."]

["The proviso stays Article IX, Section 3 (the waiting period for revised price lists) \"pending further order of the Administrator for Industrial Recovery\". The stay ends on a further order, not a date; no held source shows a further order, and a search of the held order texts for 'Photographic and Photo Finishing' finds only this order.", "A stay pending further order is a contingent command that needs its own end or a block; absence of a held further order does not show that none was issued before June 14, 1935, and an Administrator's order would not appear among held presidential orders.", "To unblock: a held record of the Administrator's order (or its absence) for Article IX, Section 3, or a reviewed ruling that the stay, as a section 3(a) exception, falls only with the approval."]

["No text of Executive Order 6756-E is held: the census register shows best held 'nothing', the page-check lookup finds no record for the original's sha256, and the only evidence is the WPA list line (1934 June 29, p.583) 'Amendments to Code of Fair Competition for the Dis tilledSpiritsRectifying Industry approved.' Held Executive Order 6756-D (Distilled Spirits Industry code) is a different order.", "Without the text no operative command, term, inventory or quotation can be established."]

["Clause 3 directs the Administrator for Industrial Recovery \"to cause a study to be made of the effects of this order ... and to report to the President thereon within six (6) months of the date of this order\" (a deadline of about December 29, 1934). A report direction is independent of the code rules, and a report date is a deadline, not an end; no held source shows that the study was made or reported.", "Clause 4 modifies all prior executive orders, including Executive Order 6646 of March 14, 1934, to the extent they conflict. Its effect on those orders is a one-time modification whose scope depends on the text of Executive Order 6646 and other orders it reaches, which the packet does not carry.", "Clause 2 delegates to the Administrator power to reduce the 15 percent tolerance after investigation; its end depends on the delegation and on whether the Administrator acted, and no held source shows either."]

["Clause 3 continues a committee (Hotchkiss, Lauck, Nelson) \"with instructions further to investigate the protests of the Sheep Lined and Leather Garment Subdivision ... and report its findings and recommendations therein on or before November 15, 1934\". Clause 4 directs the National Industrial Recovery Board to \"forthwith appoint a committee of three impartial persons\" to investigate prison-labor competition and report \"not later than December 1, 1934\". Clause 5 directs the Board to report on exemptions \"on or before January 15, 1935\". These are committees and report directions; each date is a deadline, not an end, and no held source shows the committees reporting or dissolving or the Board's report being made.", "Clause 2 (stay of the effective date of the amendments to Articles III and IV \"to and including December 1, 1934\") has an own-terms end, recorded inclusive as December 1, 1934, and clause 1 (revocation of paragraph 1 of Executive Order 6861) is exhausted on October 12, 1934, but one outcome cannot carry those ends while clauses 3 to 5 remain unresolved.", "Clause 6 (\"subject to my further orders in the premises\") is a reservation, not a command of its own."]

["Clause 3 says the members of the automobile industry \"are requested and authorized to enter into agreements with one another with respect to Fall announcements of new models ... and the holding of automobile shows\". An authorization to make agreements among competitors may rest on section 4(a) (voluntary agreements), whose authority ran to April 1, 1936 rather than ending with the section 3 repeal; the shared analysis lists section 4(a) agreements as a category it does not decide, and the order does not say which section it uses.", "Clause 4 \"confirm[s] and continue[s]\" the settlement-of-labor-controversy provisions \"established by the government and ... in operation since March 1934\". That is a labor-board arrangement resting on section 7(a) or other authority, another category the shared analysis excludes, and no held source states when it ended.", "Clause 1 sets the code's 'expiration date' at June 16, 1935, which is later than the June 14, 1935 repeal and does not move the end; clause 2 (overtime at time and one-half after 48 hours) is a code term that would end June 14, 1935."]
